2114    VALID_PROPERTIES = {
2115        "ids", "flags", "timestamp", "user", "userid", "size", "slotsize", "sha1",
2116        "slotsha1", "contentmodel", "comment", "parsedcomment", "content",
2117        "tags", "roles"
2118    }
2119    """
2120    Defines valid properties (`rvprop`) for querying revision metadata in the MediaWiki API.
2121
2122    Purpose:
2123    - Specifies which metadata fields to include in the response when fetching revisions.
2124
2125    Examples:
2126    - To fetch only revision IDs, users, and timestamps:
2127    rvprop = ["ids", "user", "timestamp"]
2128
2129    - To fetch detailed content-related fields:
2130    rvprop = ["content", "contentmodel"]
2131
2132    Warnings:
2133    - Including `content` caps `rvlimit` at 50 for performance reasons.
2134
2135    Attributes:
2136    - `ids`: Revision ID.
2137    - `flags`: Flags associated with the revision (e.g., `minor` for minor edits).
2138    - `timestamp`: Timestamp of the revision in ISO 8601 format.
2139    - `user`: Username of the revision author.
2140    - `comment`: Edit summary provided by the author, if available.
2141    """
2142
2143    DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES = {
2144        "parsetree", "rvexpandtemplates", "rvgeneratexml", "rvparse", "rvdiffto", "rvdifftotext"
2145    }
2146    """
2147    Specifies deprecated properties for querying revisions.
2148
2149    Purpose:
2150    - Retains backward compatibility with older versions of the MediaWiki API.
2151
2152    Warnings:
2153    - Deprecated properties will raise warnings when used. Replace them with the recommended alternatives.
2154
2155    Examples:
2156    - `rvexpandtemplates` → Use `action=expandtemplates`.
2157    - `rvdiffto` → Use `action=compare`.
2158    """
2159
2160    def validate_revisions_params(self, **kwargs) -> dict:
2161        """
2162        Validates and constructs parameters for querying revisions using the MediaWiki API.
2163        Ensures that parameters provided for fetching revisions conform to the MediaWiki API specifications.
2164        Detects invalid or deprecated properties and raises warnings.
2165
2166        :param kwargs: Query parameters for revisions.
2167            - **rvlimit** (int): Number of revisions to fetch. Must be between 1 and 500.
2168            - **rvprop** (list[str]): List of properties to include in the response. Must be valid properties from `VALID_PROPERTIES`.
2169            - **rvdir** (str): Direction to list revisions. Can be "newer" (oldest first) or "older" (default).
2170            - **rvstart** (str): ISO timestamp to start fetching revisions from.
2171            - **rvend** (str): ISO timestamp to stop fetching revisions at.
2172        :return: A dictionary of validated query parameters for the MediaWiki API.
2173        :raises ValueError: If an invalid parameter or value is provided, DeprecationWarning for deprecated properties.
2174
2175        .. note::
2176            - Parameters are validated against `VALID_PROPERTIES` and `DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES`.
2177            - Any deprecated properties used will raise a warning.
2178
2179        **Example Usage**::
2180
2181            validated_params = my_wrapper.validate_revisions_params(
2182                rvlimit=10,
2183                rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"],
2184                rvdir="older",
2185                rvstart="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
2186            )
2187        """
2188        params = {
2189            "action": "query",
2190            "prop": "revisions",
2191            "titles": self.title,
2192            "format": "json",
2193        }
2194
2195        if "rvlimit" in kwargs:
2196            if not 1 <= kwargs["rvlimit"] <= 500:
2197                raise ValueError("rvlimit must be between 1 and 500")
2198            params["rvlimit"] = kwargs["rvlimit"]
2199
2200        if "rvprop" in kwargs:
2201            invalid_props = set(kwargs["rvprop"]) - self.VALID_PROPERTIES - self.DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES
2202            if invalid_props:
2203                raise ValueError(f"Invalid rvprop values: {invalid_props}")
2204            deprecated_props = set(kwargs["rvprop"]) & self.DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES
2205            if deprecated_props:
2206                warnings.warn(
2207                    f"Deprecated rvprop values: {deprecated_props}. Use alternatives where possible.",
2208                    DeprecationWarning
2209                )
2210            params["rvprop"] = "|".join(kwargs["rvprop"])
2211
2212        if "rvdir" in kwargs:
2213            if kwargs["rvdir"] not in {"newer", "older"}:
2214                raise ValueError("rvdir must be either 'newer' or 'older'")
2215            params["rvdir"] = kwargs["rvdir"]
2216
2217        if "rvstart" in kwargs:
2218            params["rvstart"] = kwargs["rvstart"]
2219
2220        if "rvend" in kwargs:
2221            params["rvend"] = kwargs["rvend"]
2222
2223        return params
2224
2225
2226    def get_revisions(self, filter_substantive: bool = True, **kwargs) -> Optional[list[dict]]:
2227        """
2228        Fetches revisions for the current page using specified query parameters.
2229        Provides detailed metadata about the revisions of a Wikipedia page and optionally filters out minor edits.
2230
2231        :param filter_substantive: 
2232            If True, excludes minor edits (marked with the "minor" flag in `flags`).
2233            Minor edits typically involve formatting or other non-content changes.
2234        :param kwargs: Additional parameters validated by `validate_revisions_params`.
2235        :return: A list of revision dictionaries, each containing:
2236        - **revid**: Revision ID.
2237        - **flags**: Flags for the revision (e.g., `minor`).
2238        - **timestamp**: Timestamp of the revision.
2239        - **user**: Username of the editor.
2240        - **comment**: Edit summary, if available.
2241        :raises ValueError: If an invalid parameter or value is provided. RuntimeError if the API request fails.
2242
2243        **Example Usage**::
2244            
2245                revisions = my_wrapper.get_revisions(rvlimit=5, rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"])
2246                for rev in revisions:
2247                    print(f"Revision ID: {rev['revid']}, User: {rev['user']}, Timestamp: {rev['timestamp']}")
2248                    print(f"Comment: {rev['comment']}")
2249        """
2250        log_message = "Filtering out non-substantive edits (flagged as 'minor')." if filter_substantive else "Including all edits, including minor changes."
2251        log.info(log_message)
2252
2253        params = self.validate_revisions_params(**kwargs)
2254        raw_data = self.__query(params)
2255        pages = raw_data.get("query", {}).get("pages", {})
2256        if not pages:
2257            return []
2258
2259        page_data = next(iter(pages.values()), {})
2260        revisions = page_data.get("revisions", [])
2261
2262        if filter_substantive:
2263            revisions = [rev for rev in revisions if "minor" not in rev.get("flags", [])]
2264
2265        return revisions
2266
2267
2268    def summarize_recent_revisions(self, rvlimit: int = 5) -> list[dict]:
2269        """
2270        Summarizes recent revisions for the current page.
2271
2272        :param rvlimit: Number of recent revisions to summarize (default: 5).
2273        :return: A list of dictionaries with revision summaries (user, timestamp, comment).
2274        """
2275        revisions = self.get_revisions(rvlimit=rvlimit, rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"])
2276        return [
2277            {
2278                "revid": rev.get("revid"),
2279                "user": rev.get("user"),
2280                "timestamp": rev.get("timestamp"),
2281                "comment": rev.get("comment"),
2282            }
2283            for rev in revisions
2284        ]
2285
2286    def fetch_revision_diff(self, old_revid: int, new_revid: int) -> str:
2287        """
2288        Fetches the difference between two revisions.
2289
2290        :param old_revid: Revision ID of the older revision.
2291        :param new_revid: Revision ID of the newer revision.
2292        :return: The diff as a string.
2293        """
2294        params = {
2295            "action": "compare",
2296            "fromrev": old_revid,
2297            "torev": new_revid,
2298            "format": "json",
2299        }
2300        raw_data = self.__query(params)
2301        return raw_data.get("compare", {}).get("*", "")
2302
2303    def fetch_latest_revisions_diff(self, filter_substantive: bool = True) -> Optional[dict]:
2304        """
2305        Fetches the difference between the latest two revisions.
2306        Provides a quick comparison between the latest two revisions, enabling users to track recent changes
2307        
2308        :param filter_substantive: If True, filters non-substantive changes.
2309        :return: A dictionary containing:
2310        - `fromrev`: Older revision ID.
2311        - `torev`: Newer revision ID.
2312        - `diff`: Highlighted differences.
2313        or None if there are not enough revisions to compare.
2314        :raises RuntimeError: If the API request fails.
2315
2316        **Example Usage**::
2317            
2318                diff = my_wrapper.fetch_latest_revisions_diff(filter_substantive=True)
2319                if diff:
2320                    print(f"Changes from revision {diff['fromrev']} to {diff['torev']}:")
2321                    print(diff['diff'])
2322        """
2323        revisions = self.get_revisions(rvprop=["ids", "flags"], rvlimit=2)
2324
2325        if filter_substantive:
2326            revisions = [rev for rev in revisions if "minor" not in rev.get("flags", [])]
2327
2328        if len(revisions) < 2:
2329            return None
2330
2331        old_revid = revisions[1]["revid"]
2332        new_revid = revisions[0]["revid"]
2333        diff = self.fetch_revision_diff(old_revid, new_revid)
2334
2335        return {
2336            "fromrev": old_revid,
2337            "torev": new_revid,
2338            "diff": diff,
2339        }
2340
2341    def fetch_diffs_in_timeframe(self, start_time: str, end_time: str = None) -> list[dict]:
2342        """
2343        Fetches differences between all revisions within a specified timeframe. Allows detailed tracking of changes over a specific period.
2344
2345        :param start_time: Start timestamp in ISO format.
2346        :param end_time: Optional end timestamp. Defaults to the current time.
2347        :return: A list of dictionaries with revision differences. Each dictionary contains:
2348        - `fromrev`: Older revision ID.
2349        - `torev`: Newer revision ID.
2350        - `timestamp`: Timestamp of the newer revision.
2351        - `user`: Username of the editor.
2352        - `comment`: Edit summary, if available.
2353        - `diff`: Highlighted differences between revisions.
2354        :raises RuntimeError: If the API request fails. ValueError if there are not enough revisions to compare.
2355        
2356        **Example Usage**::
2357
2358            changes = my_wrapper.fetch_diffs_in_timeframe("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-31T23:59:59Z")
2359            for change in changes:
2360                print(f"Changes from revision {change['fromrev']} to {change['torev']} by {change['user']} at {change['timestamp']}")
2361                print(f"Edit summary: {change['comment']}")
2362                print(change['diff'])
2363        """
2364        revisions = self.get_revisions(rvstart=start_time, rvend=end_time, rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"])
2365
2366        if len(revisions) < 2:
2367            return [{"message": "Not enough revisions to calculate diffs in the specified timeframe."}]
2368
2369        if len(revisions) > 50:
2370            warnings.warn("Fetching diffs for a large number of revisions may be slow.", UserWarning)
2371
2372        changes = []
2373        for i in range(len(revisions) - 1):
2374            old_revid = revisions[i + 1]["revid"]
2375            new_revid = revisions[i]["revid"]
2376            diff = self.fetch_revision_diff(old_revid, new_revid)
2377
2378            changes.append({
2379                "fromrev": old_revid,
2380                "torev": new_revid,
2381                "timestamp": revisions[i]["timestamp"],
2382                "user": revisions[i]["user"],
2383                "comment": revisions[i].get("comment", ""),
2384                "diff": diff,
2385            })
2386
2387        return changes

Represents a Wikipedia page.

This class allows access to Wikipedia page properties and data about a given Wikipedia page. Some properties are retrieved from the Wikimedia API and cached within the object to optimize subsequent access.

Thread-safety:

  • The WikipediaPage class is designed to be thread-safe. Locks are used to ensure the integrity of the class's internal state during concurrent page field access.
  • All property methods that modify or access shared state are synchronized using thread locks.

Note:

  • Page fields fetched via API calls (e.g., pageid, links, categories) are cached and only fetched once per instance. Subsequent accesses to these fields will retrieve data from the cache, avoiding repeated API calls.
  • Access to these fields may trigger API calls upon the first access if they are not already cached.
WikipediaPage( wiki: WikipediaClient, title: str, ns: Union[Namespace, int] = <Namespace.MAIN: 0>, language: Language = <Language.EN: 'en'>, url: Optional[str] = None, page_id: Optional[int] = None)

1051        self,
1052        wiki: WikipediaClient,
1053        title: str,
1054        ns: WikiNamespace = Namespace.MAIN,
1055        language: Language = Language.EN,
1056        url: Optional[str] = None,
1057        page_id: Optional[int] = None,
1058    ) -> None:
1059        """
1060        Initializes a WikipediaPage object.
1061
1062        :param wiki: The Wikipedia API wrapper instance.
1063        :param title: The title of the page.
1064        :param ns: The namespace of the page.
1065        :param language: The language of the page, as a Language enum.
1066        :param url: Optional full URL of the page.
1067        :param page_id: Optional unique identifier for the page.
1068        """
1069        # locks to protect the following fields when methods are concurrently called
1070        self.__extract_builder_lock = threading.Lock() # protects the following
1071        self._wiki = wiki
1072        self._summary = ""  # type: str
1073        self._section = []  # type: list[WikipediaPageSection]
1074        self._section_mapping = {}  # type: dict[str, list[WikipediaPageSection]]
1075        
1076        self.__langlinks_lock = threading.Lock()
1077        self._langlinks = {}  # type: PagesDict
1078        
1079        self.__links_lock = threading.Lock()
1080        self._links = {}  # type: PagesDict
1081        
1082        self.__backlinks_lock = threading.Lock()
1083        self._backlinks = {}  # type: PagesDict
1084        
1085        self.__categories_lock = threading.Lock()
1086        self._categories = []  # type: list[str]
1087        
1088        self.__called_functions_lock = threading.Lock() # protects the following field
1089        self.__called_functions = set()
1090
1091        self._attributes = {
1092            "title": title,
1093            "ns": namespace2int(ns),
1094            "language": language,
1095            "image_url": "",
1096        }  # type: dict[str, Any]
1097
1098        if url is not None:
1099            self._attributes["fullurl"] = url
1100
1101        if page_id is not None:
1102            self._attributes["pageid"] = page_id
1103            
1104        self.ATTRIBUTES_MAPPING = {
1105        "language": [],
1106        "pageid": [self.__info, self.extracts, self.__langlinks_func],
1107        "ns": [self.__info, self.extracts, self.__langlinks_func],
1108        "title": [self.__info, self.extracts, self.__langlinks_func],
1109        "contentmodel": [self.__info],
1110        "pagelanguage": [self.__info],
1111        "pagelanguagehtmlcode": [self.__info],
1112        "pagelanguagedir": [self.__info],
1113        "touched": [self.__info],
1114        "lastrevid": [self.__info],
1115        "length": [self.__info],
1116        "protection": [self.__info],
1117        "watched": [self.__info],
1118        "restrictiontypes": [self.__info],
1119        "watchers": [self.__info],
1120        "visitingwatchers": [self.__info],
1121        "notificationtimestamp": [self.__info],
1122        "subjectid": [self.__info],
1123        "associatedpage": [self.__info],
1124        "talkid": [self.__info],
1125        "fullurl": [self.__info],

def extracts(self, **kwargs) -> str: 
1140    def extracts(self, **kwargs) -> str:
1141        """
1142        Retrieve plain-text or limited HTML extracts of specified pages. 
1143
1144        API Calls for parameters:
1145
1146        - https://www.mediawiki.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=query%2Bextracts
1147        - https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:TextExtracts#API
1148
1149        :param kwargs: parameters used in API call
1150        :return: plain-text or HTML of the page
1151
1152        """
1153        params = {
1154            "action": "query",
1155            "prop": "extracts",
1156            "titles": self.title,
1157        }  # type: dict[str, Any]
1158
1159        if self._wiki.get_extract_format() == ExtractFormat.HTML:
1160            # we do nothing, when format is HTML
1161            pass
1162        elif self._wiki.get_extract_format() == ExtractFormat.WIKI:
1163            params["explaintext"] = 1
1164            params["exsectionformat"] = "wiki"
1165
1166        used_params = kwargs
1167        used_params.update(params)
1168
1169        raw = self.__query(used_params)
1170        if 'warnings' in raw:
1171            log.warning("WARNING "+str(raw['warnings']))
1172        self.__common_attributes(raw["query"])
1173        pages = raw["query"]["pages"]
1174        for k, v in pages.items():
1175            if k == "-1":
1176                self._attributes["pageid"] = -1
1177                return ""
1178            with self.__extract_builder_lock:
1179                self.__build_extracts(v)
1180            return v["extract"]
1181        return ""

infobox: str 
2019    @property
2020    def infobox(self) -> str:
2021        """
2022        Retrieves the raw infobox wikitext of the page if present.
2023
2024        The infobox is returned as raw wikitext, allowing the client to parse
2025        it as needed. This approach provides flexibility for handling the infobox
2026        in a custom manner based on the application's requirements.
2027
2028        The raw wikitext includes: Infobox fields and values, Nested templates (if present), Any additional formatting or metadata as defined in the page content
2029            
2030        Example response::
2031
2032            {{Infobox French commune
2033            |name                   = Paris
2034            |commune status         = [[Capital city]], [[Communes of France|commune]], and [[Departments of France|department]]
2035            |image                  = {{multiple image
2036            |border            = infobox
2037            |perrow            = 1/3/2/1
2038            |total_width       = 290
2039            |caption_align = center
2040
2041        Example Usage::
2042
2043            page = wiki_client.get_page_by_title("Python (programming language)")
2044            raw_infobox = page.infobox
2045            lines = raw_infobox.split("\n")
2046            fields = {}
2047            for line in lines:
2048                if "=" in line and not line.strip().startswith("|}"):
2049                    key, value = line.split("=", 1)
2050                    fields[key.strip()] = value.strip()
2051            print(fields)
2052
2053        Note: If the page does not contain an infobox, an empty string is returned. Parsing and extracting specific fields or values should be done by the client.
2054
2055        :return: The raw wikitext of the infobox, or an empty string if not present.
2056        """
2057        params = {
2058            "action": "parse",
2059            "page": self.title,
2060            "prop": "wikitext",
2061        }
2062        raw_data = self.__query(params)
2063        wikitext = raw_data.get("parse", {}).get("wikitext", {}).get("*", "")
2064
2065        if "{{Infobox" in wikitext:
2066            infobox_start = wikitext.split("{{Infobox", 1)[1]
2067            infobox_content = []
2068            brace_stack = ["{{"]
2069
2070            for i, char in enumerate(infobox_start):
2071                infobox_content.append(char)
2072
2073                if char == '{' and i + 1 < len(infobox_start) and infobox_start[i + 1] == '{':
2074                    brace_stack.append('{{')
2075                elif char == '}' and i + 1 < len(infobox_start) and infobox_start[i + 1] == '}':
2076                    brace_stack.pop()
2077                    if not brace_stack:
2078                        infobox_content.append('}')
2079                        break
2080            print("{{Infobox" + ''.join(infobox_content))
2081            return "{{Infobox" + ''.join(infobox_content)
2082
2083        return ""

Retrieves the raw infobox wikitext of the page if present.

    The infobox is returned as raw wikitext, allowing the client to parse
    it as needed. This approach provides flexibility for handling the infobox
    in a custom manner based on the application's requirements.

    The raw wikitext includes: Infobox fields and values, Nested templates (if present), Any additional formatting or metadata as defined in the page content

    Example response::

        {{Infobox French commune
        |name                   = Paris
        |commune status         = [[Capital city]], [[Communes of France|commune]], and [[Departments of France|department]]
        |image                  = {{multiple image
        |border            = infobox
        |perrow            = 1/3/2/1
        |total_width       = 290
        |caption_align = center

    Example Usage::

        page = wiki_client.get_page_by_title("Python (programming language)")
        raw_infobox = page.infobox
        lines = raw_infobox.split("

") fields = {} for line in lines: if "=" in line and not line.strip().startswith("|}"): key, value = line.split("=", 1) fields[key.strip()] = value.strip() print(fields)

    Note: If the page does not contain an infobox, an empty string is returned. Parsing and extracting specific fields or values should be done by the client.

    :return: The raw wikitext of the infobox, or an empty string if not present.

VALID_PROPERTIES = {'timestamp', 'sha1', 'roles', 'slotsha1', 'parsedcomment', 'ids', 'comment', 'flags', 'contentmodel', 'userid', 'user', 'tags', 'size', 'slotsize', 'content'}

Defines valid properties (rvprop) for querying revision metadata in the MediaWiki API.

Purpose:

  • Specifies which metadata fields to include in the response when fetching revisions.

Examples:

  • To fetch only revision IDs, users, and timestamps: rvprop = ["ids", "user", "timestamp"]
  • To fetch detailed content-related fields: rvprop = ["content", "contentmodel"]

Warnings:

  • Including content caps rvlimit at 50 for performance reasons.

Attributes:

  • ids: Revision ID.
  • flags: Flags associated with the revision (e.g., minor for minor edits).
  • timestamp: Timestamp of the revision in ISO 8601 format.
  • user: Username of the revision author.
  • comment: Edit summary provided by the author, if available.
DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES = {'rvgeneratexml', 'rvexpandtemplates', 'rvparse', 'rvdifftotext', 'rvdiffto', 'parsetree'}

Specifies deprecated properties for querying revisions.

Purpose:

  • Retains backward compatibility with older versions of the MediaWiki API.

Warnings:

  • Deprecated properties will raise warnings when used. Replace them with the recommended alternatives.

Examples:

  • rvexpandtemplates → Use action=expandtemplates.
  • rvdiffto → Use action=compare.
def validate_revisions_params(self, **kwargs) -> dict: 
2160    def validate_revisions_params(self, **kwargs) -> dict:
2161        """
2162        Validates and constructs parameters for querying revisions using the MediaWiki API.
2163        Ensures that parameters provided for fetching revisions conform to the MediaWiki API specifications.
2164        Detects invalid or deprecated properties and raises warnings.
2165
2166        :param kwargs: Query parameters for revisions.
2167            - **rvlimit** (int): Number of revisions to fetch. Must be between 1 and 500.
2168            - **rvprop** (list[str]): List of properties to include in the response. Must be valid properties from `VALID_PROPERTIES`.
2169            - **rvdir** (str): Direction to list revisions. Can be "newer" (oldest first) or "older" (default).
2170            - **rvstart** (str): ISO timestamp to start fetching revisions from.
2171            - **rvend** (str): ISO timestamp to stop fetching revisions at.
2172        :return: A dictionary of validated query parameters for the MediaWiki API.
2173        :raises ValueError: If an invalid parameter or value is provided, DeprecationWarning for deprecated properties.
2174
2175        .. note::
2176            - Parameters are validated against `VALID_PROPERTIES` and `DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES`.
2177            - Any deprecated properties used will raise a warning.
2178
2179        **Example Usage**::
2180
2181            validated_params = my_wrapper.validate_revisions_params(
2182                rvlimit=10,
2183                rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"],
2184                rvdir="older",
2185                rvstart="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
2186            )
2187        """
2188        params = {
2189            "action": "query",
2190            "prop": "revisions",
2191            "titles": self.title,
2192            "format": "json",
2193        }
2194
2195        if "rvlimit" in kwargs:
2196            if not 1 <= kwargs["rvlimit"] <= 500:
2197                raise ValueError("rvlimit must be between 1 and 500")
2198            params["rvlimit"] = kwargs["rvlimit"]
2199
2200        if "rvprop" in kwargs:
2201            invalid_props = set(kwargs["rvprop"]) - self.VALID_PROPERTIES - self.DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES
2202            if invalid_props:
2203                raise ValueError(f"Invalid rvprop values: {invalid_props}")
2204            deprecated_props = set(kwargs["rvprop"]) & self.DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES
2205            if deprecated_props:
2206                warnings.warn(
2207                    f"Deprecated rvprop values: {deprecated_props}. Use alternatives where possible.",
2208                    DeprecationWarning
2209                )
2210            params["rvprop"] = "|".join(kwargs["rvprop"])
2211
2212        if "rvdir" in kwargs:
2213            if kwargs["rvdir"] not in {"newer", "older"}:
2214                raise ValueError("rvdir must be either 'newer' or 'older'")
2215            params["rvdir"] = kwargs["rvdir"]
2216
2217        if "rvstart" in kwargs:
2218            params["rvstart"] = kwargs["rvstart"]
2219
2220        if "rvend" in kwargs:
2221            params["rvend"] = kwargs["rvend"]
2222
2223        return params

Validates and constructs parameters for querying revisions using the MediaWiki API. Ensures that parameters provided for fetching revisions conform to the MediaWiki API specifications. Detects invalid or deprecated properties and raises warnings.

Parameters
  • kwargs: Query parameters for revisions.
    • rvlimit (int): Number of revisions to fetch. Must be between 1 and 500.
    • rvprop (list[str]): List of properties to include in the response. Must be valid properties from VALID_PROPERTIES.
    • rvdir (str): Direction to list revisions. Can be "newer" (oldest first) or "older" (default).
    • rvstart (str): ISO timestamp to start fetching revisions from.
    • rvend (str): ISO timestamp to stop fetching revisions at.
Returns

A dictionary of validated query parameters for the MediaWiki API.

Raises
  • ValueError: If an invalid parameter or value is provided, DeprecationWarning for deprecated properties.
  • Parameters are validated against VALID_PROPERTIES and DEPRECATED_PROPERTIES.
  • Any deprecated properties used will raise a warning.

Example Usage::

validated_params = my_wrapper.validate_revisions_params(
    rvlimit=10,
    rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"],
    rvdir="older",
    rvstart="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
)
def get_revisions(self, filter_substantive: bool = True, **kwargs) -> Optional[list[dict]]: 
2226    def get_revisions(self, filter_substantive: bool = True, **kwargs) -> Optional[list[dict]]:
2227        """
2228        Fetches revisions for the current page using specified query parameters.
2229        Provides detailed metadata about the revisions of a Wikipedia page and optionally filters out minor edits.
2230
2231        :param filter_substantive: 
2232            If True, excludes minor edits (marked with the "minor" flag in `flags`).
2233            Minor edits typically involve formatting or other non-content changes.
2234        :param kwargs: Additional parameters validated by `validate_revisions_params`.
2235        :return: A list of revision dictionaries, each containing:
2236        - **revid**: Revision ID.
2237        - **flags**: Flags for the revision (e.g., `minor`).
2238        - **timestamp**: Timestamp of the revision.
2239        - **user**: Username of the editor.
2240        - **comment**: Edit summary, if available.
2241        :raises ValueError: If an invalid parameter or value is provided. RuntimeError if the API request fails.
2242
2243        **Example Usage**::
2244

Fetches revisions for the current page using specified query parameters. Provides detailed metadata about the revisions of a Wikipedia page and optionally filters out minor edits.

Parameters
  • filter_substantive:
    If True, excludes minor edits (marked with the "minor" flag in flags). Minor edits typically involve formatting or other non-content changes.
  • kwargs: Additional parameters validated by validate_revisions_params.
Returns

A list of revision dictionaries, each containing:

  • revid: Revision ID.
  • flags: Flags for the revision (e.g., minor).
  • timestamp: Timestamp of the revision.
  • user: Username of the editor.
  • comment: Edit summary, if available.
Raises
  • ValueError: If an invalid parameter or value is provided. RuntimeError if the API request fails.

Example Usage::

    revisions = my_wrapper.get_revisions(rvlimit=5, rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"])
    for rev in revisions:
        print(f"Revision ID: {rev['revid']}, User: {rev['user']}, Timestamp: {rev['timestamp']}")
        print(f"Comment: {rev['comment']}")

2308        :param filter_substantive: If True, filters non-substantive changes.

2321                    print(diff['diff'])

2324
2325        if filter_substantive:

2329            return None
2330

def fetch_diffs_in_timeframe(self, start_time: str, end_time: str = None) -> list[dict]: 
2341    def fetch_diffs_in_timeframe(self, start_time: str, end_time: str = None) -> list[dict]:
2342        """
2343        Fetches differences between all revisions within a specified timeframe. Allows detailed tracking of changes over a specific period.
2344
2345        :param start_time: Start timestamp in ISO format.
2346        :param end_time: Optional end timestamp. Defaults to the current time.
2347        :return: A list of dictionaries with revision differences. Each dictionary contains:
2348        - `fromrev`: Older revision ID.
2349        - `torev`: Newer revision ID.
2350        - `timestamp`: Timestamp of the newer revision.
2351        - `user`: Username of the editor.
2352        - `comment`: Edit summary, if available.
2353        - `diff`: Highlighted differences between revisions.
2354        :raises RuntimeError: If the API request fails. ValueError if there are not enough revisions to compare.
2355        
2356        **Example Usage**::
2357
2358            changes = my_wrapper.fetch_diffs_in_timeframe("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-31T23:59:59Z")
2359            for change in changes:
2360                print(f"Changes from revision {change['fromrev']} to {change['torev']} by {change['user']} at {change['timestamp']}")
2361                print(f"Edit summary: {change['comment']}")
2362                print(change['diff'])
2363        """
2364        revisions = self.get_revisions(rvstart=start_time, rvend=end_time, rvprop=["ids", "user", "timestamp", "comment"])
2365
2366        if len(revisions) < 2:
2367            return [{"message": "Not enough revisions to calculate diffs in the specified timeframe."}]
2368
2369        if len(revisions) > 50:
2370            warnings.warn("Fetching diffs for a large number of revisions may be slow.", UserWarning)
2371
2372        changes = []
2373        for i in range(len(revisions) - 1):
2374            old_revid = revisions[i + 1]["revid"]
2375            new_revid = revisions[i]["revid"]
2376            diff = self.fetch_revision_diff(old_revid, new_revid)
2377
2378            changes.append({
2379                "fromrev": old_revid,
2380                "torev": new_revid,
2381                "timestamp": revisions[i]["timestamp"],
2382                "user": revisions[i]["user"],
2383                "comment": revisions[i].get("comment", ""),
2384                "diff": diff,
2385            })
2386
2387        return changes

Fetches differences between all revisions within a specified timeframe. Allows detailed tracking of changes over a specific period.

Parameters
  • start_time: Start timestamp in ISO format.
  • end_time: Optional end timestamp. Defaults to the current time.
Returns

A list of dictionaries with revision differences. Each dictionary contains:

  • fromrev: Older revision ID.
  • torev: Newer revision ID.
  • timestamp: Timestamp of the newer revision.
  • user: Username of the editor.
  • comment: Edit summary, if available.
  • diff: Highlighted differences between revisions.
Raises
  • RuntimeError: If the API request fails. ValueError if there are not enough revisions to compare.

Example Usage::

changes = my_wrapper.fetch_diffs_in_timeframe("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-31T23:59:59Z")
for change in changes:
    print(f"Changes from revision {change['fromrev']} to {change['torev']} by {change['user']} at {change['timestamp']}")
    print(f"Edit summary: {change['comment']}")
    print(change['diff'])
